after.en: A small blur and a halving, then a small blur and a halving again: each level does only cheap work, and each is cheaper than the last. A picture shrunk level by level like this is an image pyramid; thumbnails and multi-scale feature detection rely on it.

t.en: The server makes thousands of thumbnails a day, and the cost is the electricity bill. From this level on there is a budget.
Cost is counted per output pixel: the same part working on a picture a quarter of the size costs a quarter as much.
Your task in this level: again shrink 32×32 to 8×8, with a cost of no more than 18. Something to think about: why is a big blur expensive?

brief.en: Again shrink 32×32 to 8×8, but the cost must not exceed 18. Working on a small picture is cheaper than on a big one: on a picture a quarter of the size, the same part costs a quarter as much.

hint.en: A big blur is expensive. After halving, one pixel of the picture stands for two of the original.
